name: Finance
description: Double-entry accounting v1: owner-scoped CRUD on a chart of accounts (fin_accounts), journal headers (fin_journals) and their debit/credit lines (fin_journal_lines), and recurring-journal templates (fin_recurring), plus one report (trial balance, computed by object_finance.trial_balance() over posted journals only). Reconciled against a private predecessor-system audit, not part of this repo (its finance/ app: 'Currency, Entity ..., Account (COA hierarchy, 5 types), Journal (+lines; draft/posted; ...), JournalLine (debit-or-credit, ...), ... RecurringJournal (JSON template + frequency + auto_post)'). Journal totals (total_debits_cents/total_credits_cents/is_balanced) are COMPUTED PROPERTIES via object_finance.journal_totals(), never stamped onto a record and never enforced -- posting a journal (draft->posted, owner-gated) is a bare status flip with no balance check, matching the source's own documented weak spot exactly (reconciled against a private predecessor-system audit, not part of this repo: 'posting is a bare status flip -- balance NOT enforced at post'). There is no totals-stamping HANDLES handler in this package, unlike app-invoices' invoice_totals or app-orders' order_totals -- that absence is deliberate, not an oversight; see object_finance.py's module docstring. Deferred to a later slice, per the reconciled predecessor finance model (private source audit, not part of this repo): balance ENFORCEMENT at post (a transition guard checking is_balanced -- a real improvement over the source, tracked here, not built in this migration); auto-posting journal entries from other collections (stock moves, invoices, orders, depreciation) -- no such collection currently writes a fin_journals/fin_journal_lines row, matching the source's own gap ('journal FKs from stock/invoice/depreciation stay null -- no auto-posting integration'); the recurring-journal daemon materialization job (fin_recurring's fields are carried, the scheduled pass that reads them and creates real journals is not); profit & loss, balance sheet, and cash flow reports (same fold shape as trial_balance, addable later -- trial_balance is the only report v1 ships); statement-line bank-import reconciliation; closed/locked accounting periods; multi-currency FX (the source's JournalLine carried exchange_rate/base_amount for a line's currency to differ from its journal's; this package's lines carry only debit_cents/credit_cents in the journal's own currency -- no exchange_rate field exists here, so this is a dropped field, not a carried-but-unused one, and multi-currency journals are out of scope for v1). Chart-of-accounts entity-mode seeding (the source's Entity model auto-seeds a starter chart of accounts per books-mode) is also not built -- fin_accounts rows are created by hand like every other collection's header-only seed. Account and trial-balance detail permalinks (/accounts/{id}, /trial-balance) still need site_routes records -- not seeded by this package, same precedent as app-invoices' /invoices/{invoice_id:uuid} and app-catalog's /products/{product_id:uuid}. The journal permalink /journals/{journal_id:uuid} is now a seeded 59 detail view (site_view_render): a composed page of three generic block renderers -- an editable+deletable `detail` block (fin_journals; the draft->posted transition is now an edit to the status field in the owner's edit form, not a one-click Post button -- same make-it-basic trade as app-forum's pin/lock, guarded the same way by schemas/fin_journals.json's status transitions), a `related` block (fin_journal_lines by journal_id, RELATIONAL -- an append-only event-log of ledger postings, not embedded, per the attachability criterion), and a `form` block with fixed:{journal_id:$record_id} (Add Posting, FK locked to the page's journal). Debit/credit *_cents render through /form's built-in cents formatting on the related list, same as every other *_cents field in this codebase -- no custom code. Dropped, not carried forward: the bespoke page's live-computed total-debits/total-credits/is-balanced summary strip (object_finance.journal_totals(), folded client-side over the fetched lines) has no generic block equivalent and is not rebuilt here; a balance summary would need its own report-style block (same category as trial_balance), tracked as future work, not this migration. entity_id (65 multi-entity, already on fin_journals/fin_journal_lines) needs no special handling in the composed view -- it renders as an ordinary relation field in the generic detail/edit form. object_finance.py (journal_totals/trial_balance) lives at the repository root alongside object_records.py -- a plain importable library, not a registered object in this manifest, the same way object_records.py itself is never a package object. 0.4.0 adds `denominations`: what a unit of value is and how finely it divides. Amounts are stored as an integer count of the smallest unit and the denomination says where the decimal point goes (object_money.py) -- the generalization of this codebase's founding 'money is integer cents' rule, since cents were always USD minor units. It exists now, before more money code lands, because retrofitting a scale onto stored amounts across a dozen collections is a migration nobody wants; see plan/value-accounts-and-denominations-spec.md for the value-account layer (custody, verification, assurance) it is the foundation for. Seeded with the common fiat/crypto/stablecoin/metal units including JPY (scale 0, no minor unit) and ETH (scale 18); operators add their own -- a gift-card program, a loyalty point -- as ordinary rows. 0.5.0 adds `rates`: what one denomination was worth in another, at a moment, according to a named source -- append-only, because a rate is a historical observation, not a settable value. Rates exist to supply the number a transaction STAMPS on itself when it happens and to revalue balances at a period end; they are not a tick database. `kind` (spot/close/average/historical) is carried because accounting standards use different rates for different purposes and a system offering one number picks the wrong one somewhere. Lookups never use a rate dated after the moment being valued -- valuing yesterday with today's price silently restates history. 0.6.0 adds the two statements this package's own docstring had listed as deferred since v1: profit_and_loss() and balance_sheet(), the same posted-only owner-scoped fold shape as trial_balance() re-bucketed by each account type's sign convention, rendered at /statements. The balance sheet only balances once the period's net income is included in equity, so it is added as a DERIVED 'Current period earnings' line rather than a stored account -- a real year-end close would move it to retained earnings, which is what fin_journals' reserved kind=closing is for. And when the sheet does NOT balance the page says so in red with the exact signed difference, because an unbalanced balance sheet means the ledger is broken and rendering it as though it were fine is the single most useless thing a statement can do. 0.7.0 deletes the bespoke /accounts and /journals list page objects: both were ~80-85 lines of chrome around two generator calls with no business logic of their own (the same shape the journal permalink's bespoke page was in before its own Stage-6 retrofit), and are now seeded VIEW records over the same `list` block /notes uses.
